paragraphs: Lepi daat rabbenu haari"y za"l tzarik lomar beqabbalat shabbat shene peamim "boi kullah" beqol ram upaam achat belachash umah shello hizkiru b"tiqqunim" ella raq teren zimnin, meporash hattaam bedibre rabbenu za"l, yeayyen sham. umeporash bidbarayv ki shette peamim beqol ram, keneged chakema ubina ditzira, upaam achat belachash, keneged haddaat ditzira asher enennu mikkelal haeser sepirot, vekannizkar beshaar hakkavvanot. v"g shezzehu hattaam haamitti, im kol zeh dibre tora kepattish yepotzetz sala. venireh li, bs"d, od taam acher lepi happeshat: ki haadam tzarik leqabbel hashshabbat biqdushshat hammachashaba vehaddibbur umaaseh, dilkattechilla tzarik leshamero gam behirhur, velaken omerim shette peamim "boi kaleh" beqol ram keneged haddibbur maaseh, shehem geluyim venakerim lakkol; veomerim paam achat belachash, keneged hammachashaba shehi nisteret veenah nikrat leshum adam, ki im lah' lebaddo.

Venireh li, bs"d: "bae kaleh" oleh mispar "chayyim", diqdushshat hashshabbat hi mechayyim haelyonim, velaken lo nittena ella leyisrael diktib behu (debarim d,d): "chayyim kullekem hayyom". veyadua, tebat "hayyom" dareshu rabbotenu zikronam libraka (shabbat qyz:) al seudot hashshabbat, bitlata "hayyom" diktib beparashat beshallach. gam nireh li, besiyyata dishmayya: shelosh peamim "bae kalla" oleh mispar "tzaddiq", remez lisod tzaddiq hakkatub bemizmor hashshabbat: "tzaddiq ketamar yiprach"; umeporash sodo beshaar-hakkavvanot, yeayyen sham. gam hem mispar y"b peamim "tob", diqdushshat hashshabbat mosheket tob ly"b shibte yisrael min y"b partzupe haatzilut. gam shene peamim "bae kalla" deqol ram hem mispar "qol", upaam achat "bae kalla" delachash hu mispar "chayyim", hare "qol chayyim", vehaben zeh. gam nireh li, bs"d: "bei" oleh "ahaba", ki ot yu"d necheleqet lishne hhy"n, veaz: "bee" otiyyot "ahaba"; veomerim shelosh peamim "bee", remez, ki leet atta tzarik lehitqashsher bemiddat haahaba, bemachshaba ubedibbur ubemaaseh, ulehitracheq min hahashnaa vehammachaloqet; ukemo shekkatab haggaon chida" za"l b"moreh beetzba", ot q"m: kaalot hammincha beereb shabbat qodesh, hinneh hu et mesukkan lemachaloqet ben ish leishto uben hamsharetim, vehassitra-achara torachat harbeh lecharcher rib, vehaish hayyare yakop yitzro shello yeorer shum machaloqet vehaqpada, veadderabba, yebaqqesh shalom yeayyen sham.

Veda, ki hinneh kol adam haoseh qetata umeriba im ishto o banayv o mesharetayv, vadday nireh lo shehaddin immo, verauy larib al hammakshela sheyyatzea mittachat yadam beinyene habbayit. ak beemet, mi sheyyesh lo mocha beqadeqodo, ben yabin sheim yetze ezeh mikshol mittachat yadam, enennu naaseh meittam, veen zeh maaseh yedehem, ella hu maaseh satan kede lecharcher rib umadon baet hahi. veim hassatan omed keneged haishsha o hamsharet umakshilam beinyene habbayit, laasot dabar sheeno metuqqan lebaal habbayit; mah kocham lidchot maaseh satan? veki yesh adam sheyyukal lehillachem im hassatan ulenitztzechu? mi zeh yomar "yakoletti venitztzachtiv"? al ken kol ish mebin, kesheyyireh ezeh mikshol vechesron beinyanim shel habbayit, lo yasim ashma al ishto umesharetayv larib ittam, ella yitten el libbo hitnatztzelut hazzot shekkatabnu, ki emet hi, veaz yishtoq velo yarib attem velo yitkaes, vetob lo baolam hazzeh ubaolam habba.

Vehaish hammaskil yepaqqach enayv veyireh behahi ubda deita bindarim, dap s"v, ammud b, behahu bar babel disleq leara deyisrael, venaseb itteta vaamar lah: bashshili teren telopeche! perush, adashim; ubishshela teren mammash. limchar amar lah bashshili geriva! ubishshela shiur rab. amar lah: ayyeti li teren butzinin! perush, abattichim; vehebia lo teren sheragin. amar lah: tebare yatehon al baba! perush, al petach hechatzer; vehi haleka ushebartem al rosh baba ben butta alayv hashshalom; ayyen sham. velo katebu chakme hattalmud maaseh zo, ella lehodienu kamma tzarik haadam lihyot sabbalan, biprat bidbarim shennikshalim bahem bene beto lepi tummam, "p shehem qashim sheen teba hachameri sobelan, ki lepi mezeg vechomer haadam, haya rauy sheoto haish yekanneh viqallelenna vigareshenna al happetayyut shehiyyatah bah, veim kol zeh sabal veshamar lepiv mechissum veheshib yado measot ra. ukebar noda mah shenneemar baggemara behanak enashe dahava hassatan mitgareh bahem belel-shabbat laasot meriba gedola benehem, veiqqela rabbi meir lehatam shelosha shabbatot ad daabadu shelama, veshama sheqqara hassatan: "vay, deappeqe rabbi meir lehahu gabra mibbeteh"! nimtza, hammaqpid veoseh meriba, hu machaziq yadayv shel satan; ulehappek hu migrasho, vegeber yisrael.

clarification.explanation: According to the Ari, one should say "Come, O bride" during the acceptance of the Sabbath twice aloud and once quietly. The book of Tikkunim mentions it only twice, and the reason is explained by the Ari himself according to the esoteric tradition (the two times aloud correspond to the attributes of Chochmah and Binah, and the one quiet time to Da'at, which is not counted among the ten sefirot). Alongside this kabbalistic reason, Rabbi Yosef Chaim adds another reason according to the plain sense: one must accept the Sabbath in holiness in thought, speech, and action together — therefore it is said twice aloud, corresponding to speech and action which are visible to all, and once quietly, corresponding to thought, which is known to no one but God. He also brings several numerical allusions: in the defective spelling ("bo'i kallah"), the value equals "life" (the holiness of the Sabbath comes from the supernal life, and was therefore given only to Israel, as it is written, "You who cling to the Lord your God are all alive today"); three times "Come, O bride" equals the value of "tzaddik" (alluding to the sefirah of Yesod, "the righteous shall flourish like a palm tree"), and also equals twelve times the value of "good" (alluding to the fact that the holiness of the Sabbath draws goodness to the twelve tribes of Israel from the twelve supernal countenances); and he further distinguishes between the two expressions said aloud and the one said quietly — the two aloud instances of "Come, O bride" equal the value of "voice," and the quiet one equals the value of "life," together forming "the voice of life." He further adds that the word "bo'i" (come) itself equals the value of "love" (when the letter yud is divided into its two constituent letters heh), from which he derives that one should strengthen the attribute of love and distance oneself from strife and dispute, especially on the eve of the Sabbath before its entrance, which is a dangerous time when the evil force tries to stir up quarrels in the home. For this reason Rabbi Yosef Chaim strongly warns against getting angry or quarreling with members of the household (wife, children, servants) when some mishap occurs, but rather to attribute it to the machinations of the evil inclination and not to the intention of the household members, bringing as an example a story from the Talmud (Nedarim 66b) about a man who patiently bore his wife's misunderstandings, and another story about Rabbi Meir who calmed a quarrel that Satan had stirred up between a couple — and he concludes that one who insists on his rights and causes strife strengthens the evil force, while the patient one drives it away.
takeaways: "Come, O bride" is said twice aloud and once quietly, for both a kabbalistic reason (corresponding to Chochmah-Binah-Da'at) and a plain reason (thought-speech-action)

Numerical allusions: "bo'i kallah" in defective spelling equals "life"; three times equals "tzaddik" and also twelve times "good" (alluding to the twelve tribes); the two "aloud" plus the "quiet" equal "the voice of life"; "bo'i" equals "love"
The eve of the Sabbath near its entrance is a dangerous time for strife in the home; one must be especially careful against anger toward household members
Household mishaps should be attributed to the machinations of the evil inclination rather than blamed on household members, and one should act with patience

paragraphs: Seder qabbalat shabbat kepi dibre rabbenu haari"y za"l hu kak: hinneh bitchillat hakkol, im epshar laasot qabbalat shabbat bassadeh - mah tob umah naim, vehu metzuvveh min hammubchar; veim i epshar laasot bassadeh, tob latzet beqabbalat shabbat lechatzer bemaqom panuy umiggola, vekannizkar besha"ch, dap qsb. veek sheyyihyeh, hasseder kak: yaamod haadam veyachazor panayv keneged rucha maarab veyisgor enayv, veyasim yad hassemalit al hechazeh, veyad yamin al hassemalit, vikavven beema veyira keomed lipne hammelek leqabbel tosepet qedushshat shabbat, veyatchil lomar mizmor "habu laAdonai bene elim" kullo binima (veaach"k piyyut "leka dodi", kepi minhag yisrael), veaach"k yomar shette peamim "boi kaleh" beqol ram upaam achat belachash "boi kaleh shabbat malketa", veaach"k yomar "mizmor shir leyom hashshabbat" kullo binima, veaach"k "Adonai malak geut labesh" kullo, veaach"k yiptach enayv, vknz' beshaar hakkavvanot. vehinneh baamirat "bae kalla" nohagim haolam letzadded penehem letzad yamin shellahem veomerim "bae kalla" harishon, veaach"k metzaddedim penehem letzad semol veomerim "bae kalla" hashsheni, veaach"k nisharim zequpim kelappe maarab veomerim "bae kalla" hashshelishi belachash, umosip bazeh hashshelishi lomar "shabbat malketa" vekannizkar leel. veyesh semek letziddud yamin usemol veemtza middibre rabbenu za"l beshaar hakkavvanot, beseder qabbalat shabbat, kesheosin bachazaratam min hassadeh labbayit lehaqqip hashshulchan; veyoter mitbaer zeh milleshon morenu harab shemuel veyittol za"l b"chemdat yisrael", ketibat yad; ak besiddur rabbenu harasha"sh za"l lo nizkar inyan chazarat happanim leyamin velismol, veim kol zeh, minhag yisrael tora hu, veyesh taam vesemek leminhagam, veken rauy laasot. veotam bene adam sheosin qabbalat shabbat beholaka vehobaa, sheholekin ubain learba ruchot hammaqom, toin hem; ella tzarik sheyyaamdu kelappe maarab. veda, shessegirat haenayim beet qabbalat shabbat hu tzorek gadol veyesh bazeh sod, laken tzarik lizzaher bazeh; veraq otam bene adam shemmukrachim lomar qabbalat shabbat mittok siddur-tepilla, hem mukrachim liptoach enehem lirot basseper shebbeyadam; veen limchot beyadam baabur zeh, ukemo shekkatabti bitpillat haamida.

clarification.explanation: The order of accepting the Sabbath according to the Ari: the most preferable is to accept the Sabbath in a field, and if that is not possible, in a courtyard in an open, exposed place. The order of the recitation: stand facing west, close the eyes, the left hand on the chest and the right hand upon it, out of awe as one standing before a king, and say the psalm "Ascribe to the Lord, O sons of the mighty" (followed by the poem "Lecha Dodi" according to custom), and afterward "Come, O bride" twice aloud and once quietly, and afterward "A psalm, a song for the Sabbath day" and "The Lord reigns, He is robed in majesty" — and only then open the eyes. There is a custom to turn the face to the right on the first recitation, to the left on the second, and to remain facing west for the third, which is said quietly; this custom has a source in the words of the Ari and in the custom of Israel. One should not turn to the four directions during the acceptance of the Sabbath, but stand facing west alone. Closing the eyes is very important and carries a matter of the esoteric tradition (a kabbalistic depth not further detailed), but one who must read from a prayer book may open his eyes.
takeaways: The most preferable place to accept the Sabbath is a field, and failing that, an open courtyard, facing west
The order: "Ascribe to the Lord, O sons of the mighty" / "Lecha Dodi" → "Come, O bride" (twice aloud, once quietly) → "A psalm, a song for the Sabbath day" → "The Lord reigns, He is robed in majesty"
Closing the eyes during the acceptance of the Sabbath is important and carries a kabbalistic secret; one who must read from a prayer book may open his eyes for that purpose

paragraphs: Belel-shabbat yesh leadam shelosha mine tosepet shabbat: haechad tosepet nepesh, vezeh naasa beet qabbalat-shabbat beomero "bee kaleh"; vehashsheni tosepet harucha, vezeh naaseh beet sheomerim "bareku" qodem arbit; vehashshelishi tosepet hanneshama, vezeh naaseh beet sheomerim "uparush alenu veal yerushalayim ireka sukkat rachamim veshalom"; veellu hem bechinat hallayla shel shabbat, dehaynu shehem mitztzad hammalkut shezzeman aliyyatah hu belel-shabbat. ak beyom shabbat yesh od shelosha mine tosepet shel bechinat hayyom, vehem yoter meulen, shehu mitztzad hattiperet shehu yoter elyon, shehu sod dukera; ushelosha ellu nibaram leqamman, bashshabbat habbaa b"h. velaken beet qabbalat-shabbat, beamerek "boi kaleh veku'" shehu iqqar qabbalat-shabbat, tekavven leqabbel tosepet hannepesh, ubaamirat "bareku" tekavven leqabbel tosepet harucha. umeporash besiddur rabbenu harasha"sh sheqqabbalat tosepet harucha tihyeh baaniyyat "bareku", dehaynu, kaasher oneh veomer "baruk Adonai hamborak leolam vaed"; yeayyen sham. umikkol maqom, meet sheomer baal haqqaddish "bareku et Adonai hamborak", yekavven hashshomea lehakin atzmo leqabbala zo; veken zeh haomer haqqaddish atzmo, gam ken iqqar qabbalat harucha etzlo kesheomer "baruk Adonai hamborak". vekatebu beshem rabbenu harab chayyim veyittol za"l, shetztzarik haadam lihyot omed b"qaddish bareku", kede leqabbel tosepet harucha meummad; veken tzarik laqum kesheomer "uparush", kede leqabbel tosepet hanneshama meummad; venimtza sheim lo yitpallel betzibbur, deeno shomea "baraku" veoneh, hinneh hu mapsid qabbala zo; mihu, tob lomar hayyachid barayta zo: amar rabbi aqiba: chayya achat omedet baraqia ushemah "yisrael", vechaquq al mitzchah "yisrael". omedet beemtza haraqia veomeret: "bareku et Adonai hamborak", vekol gedude maala onim veomerim: "baruk Adonai hamborak leolam vaed"; ad kan. v"g dela toil barayta zo bimqom aniyyat "bareku" deqaddish mammash - leinyan zeh detosepet, mikkol maqom mehanneya purta; veleenos bitpillat yachid, tehanne leh, ki Adonai lo yimna tob laholekim betamim.

clarification.explanation: On Sabbath night a person receives three kinds of "additional measure" of the Sabbath: (1) the additional nefesh — during the acceptance of the Sabbath, in saying "Come, O bride"; (2) the additional ruach — in saying "Barchu" before the evening prayer; (3) the additional neshamah — in saying "and spread over us... a shelter of peace and mercy." These belong to the aspect of the night (from the side of Malchut, whose time of ascent is Sabbath night); and on the Sabbath day there are three more, higher ones (from the side of Tiferet). Therefore, in saying "Come, O bride" (the essence of accepting the Sabbath) one should intend to receive the additional nefesh, and in saying "Barchu" — the additional ruach (the Rashash: in answering "Blessed is the Lord who is blessed"); from the moment the leader of the Kaddish says "Barchu," the listener should prepare himself. Rabbi Chaim Vital wrote that one should stand for "Kaddish and Barchu" (to receive the ruach while standing), and likewise rise for "and spread" (to receive the neshamah while standing). It follows that one who prays alone and does not hear "Barchu" loses out on this reception; nevertheless it is good for the individual to say the beraita, "Rabbi Akiva said: there is a creature standing in the firmament called Israel... it says, 'Bless the Lord who is blessed,' and all the heavenly hosts answer, 'Blessed is the Lord who is blessed forever and ever'" — for even though this does not substitute exactly for answering "Barchu," it helps somewhat, and for one who is forced to pray alone it will be of help.
takeaways: On Sabbath night there are three additional measures: nefesh ("Come, O bride"), ruach ("Barchu"/answering "Blessed is the Lord who is blessed"), neshamah ("and spread... a shelter of peace and mercy") — and one intends to receive them

It is good to stand for "Kaddish and Barchu" and for "and spread" (to receive them while standing); one praying alone should say the beraita of "there is a creature... bless the Lord who is blessed," which helps somewhat

paragraphs: Im shakach velo kivven leqabbel tosepet harucha b"bareku" harishon, o shello shama mibbaal haqqaddish kede sheyyaaneh vikavven, yesh lo taqqana lekavven beqabbalat tosepet harucha b"bareku" haacharon sheomerim achar haamida qodem "alenu leshabbeach", veaz yeqabbel otah shaa tosepet harucha vetosepet hanneshama beyachad, yaan ki meachar dela qibbel harucha b"bareku" harishon, i epshar leqabbel tosepet hanneshama beamero "uperesh", velaken atta yekavven leqabbel shenehem yachad, vekannizkar bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l beshaar hakkavvanot.

clarification.explanation: One who forgot to intend to receive the additional ruach at the first "Barchu" (before the evening prayer), or did not hear it from the prayer leader in order to answer and intend it — has a remedy: he can intend to receive the additional ruach at the final "Barchu," said after the Amidah, before "Aleinu leshabeach." In this case he receives, at that same time, both the additional ruach and the additional neshamah together, since, having not received the ruach at the first "Barchu," he could not have received the additional neshamah at the earlier saying of "and spread" — and so now he intends to receive both together. This is explained in the words of the Ari.
takeaways: One who missed intending the additional ruach at the first "Barchu" should intend it at the final "Barchu" after the Amidah
He then receives both the additional ruach and the additional neshamah together

paragraphs: Piyyut "leka dodi" lo nizkar bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l, ki zeh happiyyut chibbero rabbenu shelomoh elqabbetz za"l, veen chiyyub baamirato, ak pashat hamminhag leamero; abal amirat "bae kalla bae kalla, bae kalla shabbat malketa" hi middibre rabbotenu za"l, venizkera baggemara ubetiqqunim. ukepi dibre rabbenu haari"y za"l, iqqar qabbalat-shabbat hi beamero "bee kaleh", veaz neesar baasiyyat melaka "p shello amar adayin "mizmor shir leyom hashshabbat". umah shekkatab maran za"l beshulchano hattahor (siman rs, seip d) deneesar baasiyyat melaka mishsheyyatchil lomar "mizmor shir leyom hashshabbat", haynu, mippene shebbeyamayv lo nitpashshetu dibre rabbenu haari"y za"l, o yittaken dehaya minhagam lomar "bae kalla" achar amirat hammizmor. vaanachnu, en lanu ella dibre rabbenu haari"y za"l deqabbalat-shabbat chala baamirat "bae kalla", veken katab harab "halakot qetannot", diksheomer "bee kalla" qabbeleh leshabbat veasur bimlaka; yeayyen sham. veda, ki beyom tob, chal alehem qedushshat yom tob baamirat "bareku" deqodem arbit, venakon lehachmir meamirat hammizmor.

clarification.explanation: The poem "Lecha Dodi" is not mentioned in the words of the Ari, since it was composed by Rabbi Shlomo Alkabetz, and there is no obligation to say it even though the widespread custom is to say it. By contrast, saying "Come, O bride, come, O bride, come, O bride, the Sabbath queen" is from the words of the Sages themselves, and is mentioned in the Talmud and in the Tikkunim. According to the Ari, the essential acceptance of the Sabbath takes effect already at the saying of "Come, O bride," and from that moment doing work is forbidden — even before one has said "A psalm, a song for the Sabbath day." What Maran wrote in the Shulchan Aruch, that the prohibition takes effect only from the beginning of "A psalm, a song for the Sabbath day," is because in his time the words of the Ari had not yet spread, or because their custom was to say "Come, O bride" only after the psalm. But we follow the words of the Ari, that acceptance takes effect already at "Come, O bride." Regarding a festival, its holiness takes effect at the saying of "Barchu" before the evening prayer, and it is proper to be stringent already from the saying of the psalm.
takeaways: "Lecha Dodi" is not obligatory (a custom only); "Come, O bride" comes from the Sages and is when the acceptance of the Sabbath actually takes effect
From the moment "Come, O bride" is said, doing work is already forbidden, following the Ari, whom we follow in this practice
On a festival, holiness takes effect at "Barchu"; it is proper to be stringent already from the psalm

paragraphs: Chayyab adam lehosip mechol al haqqodesh, uzeman tosepet zeh, yesh bo kamma sebarot chaluqot; vaanachnu, en lanu ella dibre rabbenu haari"y za"l sheamar: zeman qabbalat-shabbat hu samuk lishqiat hachamma. ubearnu kavvanato - rotzeh lomar, keshehachamma berosh hailanot, dehaynu shelish shaa qodem qeriat ha"magreb" sheqqore besop shaa y"b mammash. vehamacher lomar qabbalat shabbat ben-hashshemashot, shemmatchil shiba deqim vachetzi qodem qeriat ha"miggarab", hipsid mitzvat hattosepet. umeporash lehedya bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l beshaar hakkavvanot, dap tz"z, "b, deen niqra tosepet ella im ken nimsheka qodem zemannah harauy lah, abal kesheyyitqaddesh hashshabbat atzmo veyihyeh mammash lel-shabbat gemura, eno niqra tosepet, raq qedushshat shabbat atzmo; yeayyen sham. mihu, kol zeh al qabbalat-shabbat baamirat "bee kaleh", abal "qaddish bareku" shebbo tosepet harucha, veken amirat "uparush" shebbah tosepet hanneshama eno tzarik sheyyihyeh zeh bevadday yom, ella "p shennaasa layla, en bekak kelum. veken nireh lehedya beshaar hakkavvanot, dap tz"t, ammud g, sherabbenu haari"y za"l beatzmo haya oseh kol zeh achar shennaasa layla mammash.

clarification.explanation: There is an obligation to add from the profane to the holy (to bring forward the acceptance of the Sabbath before its actual time), and there are various opinions as to exactly when this period begins. Rabbi Yosef Chaim rules like the Ari, that the time for accepting the Sabbath is close to sunset — that is, when the sun is still "at the tops of the trees," which is about a third of an hour before the call to "Maghrib" (the Muslim call to the evening prayer, used here as a time marker, called close to sunset). Twilight itself begins about seven and a half minutes before the call to Maghrib. One who delays saying the acceptance of the Sabbath until twilight itself (right before sunset) has lost the commandment of the addition. According to the Ari in Sha'ar HaKavanot, only what is done before the proper time is called an "addition"; but if the Sabbath has already actually taken effect, this is already the holiness of the Sabbath itself and not an addition. However, all this concerns only the acceptance of the Sabbath through saying "Come, O bride"; by contrast, "Barchu" (the additional ruach) and "and spread" (the additional neshamah) may be said even once it has actually become night, as the Ari himself was accustomed to do.
takeaways: There is an obligation to bring forward the acceptance of the Sabbath before its actual time (the addition to the Sabbath), set at about a third of an hour before actual sunset
One who delays until twilight itself loses the commandment of the addition in the acceptance of the Sabbath itself
"Barchu" and "and spread" (the additional ruach and neshamah) are valid even once it has actually become night

paragraphs: Mi sheqqibbel shabbat mibbeod yom, yukal lomar lachabero shello qibbel shabbat adayin, laasot ezeh melaka; veayyen "machaziq beraka" ushear acharonim; mihu, harab "chesed laalapim" za"l hebi mitteshubat "bayit chadash" za"l, denakon lehachmir bazeh, yeayyen sham. venireh li diltzorek metzuvveh yesh lehaqel velo lehachmir, veken hamminhag pashut.

clarification.explanation: One who has already accepted the Sabbath upon himself while it is still day may tell his friend, who has not yet accepted the Sabbath, to do a certain task for him (since for the friend it is still a weekday). Some hold that it is proper to be stringent and not say this. But Rabbi Yosef Chaim holds that for the sake of a commandment one should be lenient rather than stringent, and this is the widespread custom.
takeaways: One who accepted the Sabbath early may tell his friend, who has not yet accepted it, to do a task for him
For the sake of a commandment, one should be lenient about this, and this is the actual custom

paragraphs: Im taa bearbit deshabbat vehitchil tepillat chol venizkar beemtza habberaka, gomer otah beraka veyachazor lomar shel shabbat. vezeh haddin yeshno gam bitpillat shacharit umincha, abal im taa bemusap, poseq apillu beemtza habberaka velo yigmerenna, ella yatchil shel shabbat tekep. umeporash bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l: bearbit yomar "veyanuchu bah", ubeshacharit "veyanuchu bo", ak bemincha lo nitparesh bidbarayv kelum. vegam besiddur rabbenu harasha"sh lo nitparesh al mincha. veshamati deminhag hachasidim beare haqqodesh t"v lomar bemincha "bo", ak anachnu, minhagenu lomar bemincha "bam" kemo shekkatab hrm"z za"l v"mishnat-chasidim" za"l.

clarification.explanation: One who erred in the Sabbath evening prayer and mistakenly began with the weekday text, and remembered in the middle of the blessing, should finish that blessing as he began it, and only then return to the Sabbath text. The same law applies to the morning and afternoon prayers. But in the additional (Musaf) prayer, if he erred, he stops immediately even in the middle of the blessing and does not finish it, but immediately begins the Sabbath text. Regarding the exact wording to add in the blessing of rest: in the evening prayer one says "and let them rest in it" (feminine form), in the morning prayer "and let them rest in it" (masculine form) — as explained in the words of the Ari — but for the afternoon prayer no explicit wording was transmitted, either from the Ari or from the Rashash. Some are accustomed to say the masculine form in the afternoon prayer as well, but the custom accepted by Rabbi Yosef Chaim is to say the plural form, "and let them rest in them."
takeaways: Mistakenly starting the weekday text in the evening, morning, or afternoon prayer of the Sabbath — one finishes the blessing already begun and then returns to the Sabbath text
In the Musaf prayer — one stops immediately, even mid-blessing, and returns to the Sabbath text
The wording of "rest": evening — feminine form; morning — masculine form; afternoon — according to our custom, the plural form

paragraphs: Achar tepillat arbit omerim "vaykullu" beqol ram meummad, vaapillu hammitpallel beyachid chayyab leomero, sheyyesh sod amoq baamirat shelosh peamim "vaykullu", veen ligroa mehem apillu beyachid.

clarification.explanation: After the evening prayer, "Vayechulu" is said aloud and standing, and this obligation applies even to one who prays alone. The reason: there is a deep secret in saying "Vayechulu" three times (as customary, both for the individual and for the congregation), and therefore one should not forgo it even when praying alone.
takeaways: "Vayechulu" is said aloud and standing, whether alone or with a congregation
There is a deep secret in saying it three times, and therefore one should not forgo it

paragraphs: Beraka meen sheba, en iqqar taam shellah hu mah sheameru rabbotenu za"l shennitqena bishbil hamacharin bebet-hakkeneset shebbassadeh, ella beemet yesh bah tzorek gadol al pi hassod, vehu bimqom hachazara. laken, gam im mitpallelin tzibbur bebet chatanim vaabelim vekayyotze, sheen sham seper tora, chayyabin lomar beraka meen sheba, veken pashat hamminhag birushalayim leomerah bekol maqom shemmitpallelim baasara, "p sheen sham seper tora; vezeh hamminhag nitpashshet mizzeman rabbenu harasha"sh za"l, ukemo shekkatab beseper "peri-haadama", veken hinhagti poh irenu y" beezrat Adonai yitbarek.

clarification.explanation: The blessing of "Mei'ein Sheva" (the abbreviated blessing the cantor recites on Sabbath night at the end of the evening prayer) does not have, as its primary reason (as some of the Sages held), only the purpose of delaying the latecomers in the synagogue that was in the field (out of concern for danger on the way back), but has a deeper purpose according to the esoteric tradition — it comes in place of the "repetition of the Amidah" (the leader's repetition of the prayer). Because of this, it should be said even when the congregation prays in a place that has no Torah scroll (such as a wedding hall or a house of mourning), and this is the widespread custom in Jerusalem — to say it wherever a minyan prays, even without a Torah scroll — a custom that spread from the time of the Rashash, and which Rabbi Yosef Chaim himself practiced in his city of Baghdad.
takeaways: "Mei'ein Sheva" is said because it stands in place of the repetition of the Amidah (a kabbalistic reason), not only because of latecomers
Therefore it is said even in a minyan without a Torah scroll, as is the custom in Jerusalem and in Baghdad

paragraphs: Achar tepilla yelek lebeto tekep umiyyad leqaddesh. veseder haqqiddush katabti leel bs"d. umiyyad achar haqqiddush yaaseh netilat yadayim kehilkatah mikkeli sheeno naqub. veqodem sheyyittol yadayv yomar "mizmor ledavid, Adonai roi lo echsar" sheyyesh bo z"n tebot, vikavven shello yechsar mezono vegam mezon hannepesh, vekannizkar besiddur rabbenu harasha"sh za"l. veyesh nohagim leamero achar netilat yadayim, veen limchot beyadam, vekannizkar b"machaziq beraka", siman qs"v. gam qodem sheyyittol yadayv yomar nosach zeh: leshem yichud qudesha berik hu veku', hareni ba leqayyem mitzvat aseh derabbanan littol yaday uleshapshepam qodem seuda, kede laasot nachat rucha leyotzeri velaasot retzon borei letaqqen shoresh metzuvveh zo bemaqom elyon. vihi ratzon millepaneka Adonai elohenu velohe abotenu, shettihyeh chashuba umequbbelet uretzuya lepaneka metzuvveh zo shel netilat yadayim vehashshipshup qodem seuda keillu kivvanti bekol hakkavvanot hareuyot lekavven bimtzuvva zo. vihi ratzon millepaneka Adonai elohenu velohe abotenu, shebbizkut mitzvat habberaka asher nebarek al netilat yadayim qodem seuda, yihyeh atta et ratzon lepaneka, veyimmashek min or en sop shepa mochin veorot gedolim lishnayim-asar partzupim haremuzim beeser sepirot hakkolelim, haremuzim beeser etzbaot hayyadayim, umishsham neqabbel shepa esreh berakot kakkatub (bereshit kz, kch): "veyitten leka haelohim (limshok meen sop mochin veshepa) mittal hashshamayim (chakema) umishmanne haaretz (bina), verob dagan (daat) vetirosh (chesed); yaabduk ammim (gebura) veyishtachavu leka leummim (tiperet) have gebir (netzach) leachika (hod) veyishtachavvu leka bene immeka (yesod); avrarek arur umebarekeka baruk (malkut)".

clarification.explanation: After the prayer one should go straight home to recite Kiddush (the order of Kiddush was explained above), and immediately after Kiddush he should wash his hands according to halachah, from a vessel that has no hole in it. Before washing he should say "A psalm of David: the Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want" (which has 57 words), intending that his food and the food of his soul not be lacking (the Rashash); some are accustomed to say it after washing, and one should not protest against them. He should also say, before washing, the formula: "For the sake of the union of the Holy One, blessed be He... behold I come to fulfill the rabbinic positive commandment to wash my hands and rub them before the meal... and may it be Your will... that in the merit of the commandment of the blessing we recite over washing the hands, there be drawn from the light of the Infinite an abundance of intellects and great lights to the twelve countenances... alluded to in the ten fingers of the hands, and from there we shall receive an abundance of ten blessings as it is written: 'And may God give you of the dew of heaven and of the fatness of the earth, and abundance of grain and wine...'" — each part of the verse corresponds to a sefirah (the dew of heaven = Chochmah, the fatness of the earth = Binah, abundance of grain = Da'at, wine = Chesed, "let peoples serve you" = Gevurah, "and nations bow down to you" = Tiferet, "be lord" = Netzach, "over your brothers" = Hod, "and let your mother's sons bow down to you" = Yesod, "cursed be those who curse you and blessed be those who bless you" = Malchut).
takeaways: After the prayer: one recites Kiddush immediately, and after Kiddush washes the hands from a vessel with no hole; before washing he says "A psalm of David: the Lord is my shepherd" (57 words), intending that his food and the food of his soul not be lacking

He says "For the sake of the union" before washing, intending that abundance be drawn to the ten fingers and that he receive an abundance of ten blessings (as in the verse "And may God give you...", corresponding to the ten sefirot)

paragraphs: Beshabbat tzarik littol yadayv qodem shalosh seudot meummad kannizkar bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l. vehu haddin libraka veniggub name tzarik meummad. vekatab harab haggaon morenu rabbi eliyyahu minni nr"v, delav davqa bintila daakila, ella gam bintilat shacharit deyom shabbat, gam ken notelin umebarekin umenaggebim meummad, shekken katab rabbenu harasha"sh za"l, ukebar harab "torat-chakam" za"l asa matammim laddabar. vekatab od, shehu nr"v noheg gam-ken beyom tob, deim eno moil eno mazziq; ad kan debarayv nr"v. venireh li: "yapeh amar chanan" (reeh ketubbot qh.) al yom tob, ak ana abada i epshar li laasot nt"y deshacharit deshana meummad, vehammishtaddel leqayyem zeh tabo alayv beraka.

clarification.explanation: On the Sabbath one must wash the hands before each of the three meals while standing, according to the words of the Ari, and the same law applies to the blessing and the drying of the hands — these too must be done standing. Rabbi Eliyahu Mani wrote that one should stand not only for the washing before a meal, but also for the washing of the hands on Sabbath morning, as explained in the Rashash, and he practiced this on festivals as well. However, Rabbi Yosef Chaim notes that he himself is not accustomed to do this for the morning washing throughout the year (that is, on weekdays), but one who is careful about this even on a festival — blessing will come upon him.
takeaways: On the Sabbath one washes the hands, recites the blessing, and dries the hands standing, before each of the three meals
Some are accustomed to stand also for the morning washing on the Sabbath and on festivals, though Rabbi Yosef Chaim himself did not do so on weekdays

paragraphs: Kesheyyittol yadayv lasseuda yiqqach hakkeli beyado hayyemanit veyittenehu leyado hassemalit, kede lehaknia hassemalit leyamin; veyittol min hassemalit al hayyamin shelosh peamim retzupim zeh achar zeh, veaach"k yittol al hassemalit gam ken shelosh peamim retzupim bezeh achar zeh, veaach"k yeshapshep yadayv zeh bazeh, shelosh peamim retzupim leyad yamin veshalosh peamim retzupim leyad semol vekannizkar besiddur rabbenu harasha"sh za"l. v"g ki bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l, beshaar taame hammitzvot, dap n"b, ammud b, zeker bintila shette peamim, ubeshipshup paam achat - neeman rabbenu harasha"sh bazeh, shekkol debarayv haya motzi otam umolidam middibre rabbenu haari"y za"l beatzmo.

clarification.explanation: In washing the hands for the meal: one takes the vessel in the right hand and passes it to the left hand, in order to subordinate the left to the right. One pours from the left hand onto the right three times in succession, and then pours from the right hand (which now holds the vessel) onto the left three times in succession, and then rubs the hands against each other — three times for the right hand and three times for the left, as the Rashash was accustomed to do. Although the words of the Ari himself mention pouring only twice and rubbing once, Rabbi Yosef Chaim relies on the version of the Rashash, since all his words were learned directly from the words of the Ari.
takeaways: The order of washing: pour from the left onto the right three times, then from the right onto the left three times, then rub each hand three times
One follows the custom of the Rashash (three-three), not what is mentioned elsewhere in the name of the Ari (two and one)

paragraphs: Achar netilat yadayim yagbihha yadayv keneged rosho vibarek tekep umiyyad beod yadayv zequpim, kede shello tihyeh hagbahat yado bereqaneya. ubeod yadayv zequpim, yipshot yadayv sheyyesh bahem asar etzbaot, leqabbel shepa uberaka meeser mine shepa, vikavven lehamshik mimmaqom elyon mochin veshepa, vehem eser mine berakot hannizkarim bappasuq: "veyitten leka haelohim veku'" ad "umebarekeka baruk" vknz' besiddur rabbenu harasha"sh za"l. upiyyut "lemibtza al ripta", veyesh nohagim leamero achar netila, qodem betzia, ukemo shekkatab haggaon "machaziq beraka", siman qs"v, al minhag rabbanan qaddishe; yeayyen sham. ubebetenu nohagim meabotenu leamero achar netila, qodem "hammotzi"; vetzarik leamero beshalosh seudot.

clarification.explanation: After washing the hands, one raises them toward the head and immediately recites the blessing "Concerning the washing of the hands" while the hands are still raised, so that the raising of the hands not be "empty" (without an accompanying blessing). While the hands are raised and spread out, with the ten fingers, one intends to receive an abundance and blessing of ten kinds of abundance from the supernal place, corresponding to the ten kinds of blessings listed in the verse "And may God give you..." through "and blessed be those who bless you." Some are accustomed to say the poem "Lemevatzeia al Refta" after washing and before cutting the bread, as was the custom of important rabbis; Rabbi Yosef Chaim notes that this was the custom in his home — to say it at all three meals, after washing, before "Hamotzi."
takeaways: After washing, the blessing is recited immediately while the hands are still raised and spread, with the intention of receiving abundance corresponding to the ten kinds of blessing
It is customary to say the poem "Lemevatzeia al Refta" after washing and before "Hamotzi," at all three meals

paragraphs:
Tzarik libtzoa al shette kikkarot bekol seuda mishshalosh seudot, veyihyu shelemot zeker lamman diktib bah (shemot tz,kb): "lechem mishneh". vegam hannashim, im okelim lebaddam, chayyabim g"k bishte kikkarot vekannizkar bapposeqim za"l; mihu, lepi daat rabbenu haari"y za"l tzarik lesadder bashshulchan shettem-esreh kikkarot bekol seuda mishshalosh seudot (shishsha zugot shehem y"b) kazeh:

ubearba kikkarot haemtzaim yekavven shehem keneged arba otiyyot shem havaya"h baruk hu, ushettayim haelyonot hem keneged ot yu"d veot va"v, shehem otiyyot hazzekarim, ushettayim shettachtehem, hem keneged shene hahin, shehem otiyyot hanneqebot: he" rishona tachat avvat yu"d shebbetzad yamin, vehe" acharona tachat ot va"v shebbetzad semol. ukeshettebarek birkat "hammotzi", tiqqach b' kikkarot haelyonot, shehem keneged otiyyot yo"d va"v, utechabberem yachad debuqim achor beachor, ubazeh naasim kikkar echad sheyyesh lo shene panim mishshene tzedadayv, sheyyihyeh bazeh kedimyon lechem-happanim shebbammiqdash; vetochazem ben shette yadeka, shettihyeh yemineka al pene kikkar hayyo"d usemoleka al pene kikkar havva"v, ubeod shette kikkarot ellu beyadeka, tzarik sheyyihyu munnachim beyadeka keneged b' kikkarot hattachtonim, shehem keneged shette hahin, kede sheyyashpiu hazzekarim banneqebot; utebarek az birkat "hammotzi" beodam ben yadeka. veachar shettigmor habberaka, tibtza millechem haymani, shehu keneged ot yu"d, shiur kazzayit, utetabbelenu shelosha peamim bemelach vetoklennu, vetikkavvan leshem mitzvat seudat shabbat, vegam tekavven dikzayit zeh hu keneged ot yu"d deshem hvy"h. veachar shettokal vetitom mikkazzayit zeh, az tekep tibtza od mikkikkar hannizkar shiur kabbetza vetitten leishteka, utekavven ki zeh hu keneged ot yu"d shel shem dn"y, utekavven az leshem hashshillub shel hvy"h dn"y, shehu shem yhdvnh"y. vehu haddabar asher yasad rabbenu haari"y za"l bepiyyut shello: "lemibtza al ripta, kezeta ukebeata, teren yodin naqeta, setimin uperishin". aach"k tibtza lishar hamsubbin. vetizzaher beet shettebatztzea et kazzayit shelleka vekabbetza shel ishteka, shello teshammet kikkar hashsheni, shehu keneged ot va"v, miyyadeka, ella tibtza beodo mechubbar beyadeka im oto kikkar sheatta botzea mimmennu. veseder zeh taasehu beshalosh seudot. veim lo nimtza leka y"b kikkarot, tesadder arba kikkarot, ak vadday metzuvveh rabba lehishtaddel lesadder y"b kikkarot kepi hatztziyyur sherishshamnu leel; veseder zeh hu hamyussad "p dibre rabbenu haari"y haqqadosh zlh"h kannizkar beshaar hakkavvanot.

clarification.explanation: At each of the three Sabbath meals one must cut from two whole loaves, in remembrance of the "double bread" (lechem mishneh) that fell with the manna in the wilderness; even women eating alone are obligated in the two loaves. However, according to the Ari, it is proper to arrange twelve loaves on the table at each meal (six pairs), arranged in a particular way: the four middle loaves correspond to the four letters of the Name YHVH, the two upper loaves correspond to the letters yud and vav (the masculine letters), and the two lower loaves correspond to the two letters heh (the feminine letters). At the blessing of "Hamotzi," one takes the two upper loaves (yud and vav), joins them back to back into one loaf with two sides (resembling the showbread in the Temple), and holds them — the right hand corresponding to the loaf of yud, the left hand to the loaf of vav — directly over the two lower loaves (the heh's), so that the masculine influences the feminine. After the blessing, one cuts an olive's-worth from the right-hand loaf (yud), dips it in salt three times, and eats it with the intention of the commandment of the Sabbath meal and of the letter yud in the Name YHVH; then one cuts an additional egg's-worth and gives it to the wife, with the intention of the letter yud in the Name Adonai (the combination Yah-Adonai). One must be careful that the second loaf (vav) remains held in the hand while cutting from the first. If there are no twelve loaves, four suffice, but it is preferable to make the effort to have twelve, according to the order of the Ari.
takeaways: The basic obligation: two whole loaves at each Sabbath meal (also for women eating alone)
According to the Ari, it is preferable to have twelve loaves, arranged to allude to the Name YHVH and to masculine and feminine, joined at "Hamotzi" like the showbread
If there are no twelve loaves, four suffice

paragraphs: Shiur kazzayit hu tisha deraham, veshiur kabbetza hu shemona-asar deraham. veachar shettebatztzea shiur kazzayit leatzmeka, tizzaher leekol od min happat lehashlim shiur tisha-asar deraham, ki tzarik leekol lekattechilla pat bisudat shabbat yoter mikkabbetza, veraq mi shehu choleh ubaal makobim deqasheh lo akilat happat, saggi leh bikzayit bilbad. veayyen b"birke-yosep" v"shiyyure beraka" ushear acharonim za"l.

clarification.explanation: The measure of an olive's-worth is nine dirhams, and the measure of an egg's-worth is eighteen dirhams. After cutting an olive's-worth for himself, one should continue eating bread until reaching a measure of nineteen dirhams, since as the primary practice one should eat more than an egg's-worth of bread at the Sabbath meal. Only one who is ill or has difficulty eating bread may content himself with just an olive's-worth.
takeaways: At the Sabbath meal one should, as the primary practice, eat more than an egg's-worth of bread (19 dirhams), not just an olive's-worth
One who is ill or has difficulty eating bread may content himself with an olive's-worth alone

paragraphs: Kaasher tesadder haishsha happat al hashshulchan, tizzaher lehannicha mappa tachtona umappa elyona; veyesh bazeh kamma teamim al pi happeshat. veachar shettannicha mappa haelyona, tannicha shette yadeha al hashshulchan vetomar pasuq: "vaydabber elay, zeh hashshulchan asher lipne Adonai", v"y dibbur zeh tishreh haqqedushsha al hashshulchan vekannizkar beseper "keter-malkut"; umistabbera milleta, kemo sheameru al kisse eliyyahu hannabi zakur lattob bishat hammila, shetztzarik lomar bappeh "zeh hakkisse veku'"; veayyen bazzohar haqqadosh (, rt:).

clarification.explanation: When the woman arranges the bread on the table, a lower cloth and an upper cloth should be placed, and there are several reasons for this according to the plain sense. After placing the upper cloth, one places both hands on the table and says the verse, "And He said to me, this is the table that is before the Lord" — and saying this verse aloud causes holiness to rest upon the table, similar to the custom of saying "This is the chair" over the chair of Elijah the Prophet at a circumcision.
takeaways: A lower cloth and an upper cloth are placed on the Sabbath table
Saying "this is the table that is before the Lord" aloud, with the hands on the table, causes holiness to rest upon it — similar to "this is the chair" at a circumcision

paragraphs: Metzuvveh leekol dagim bishlosha seudot shel shabbat, apillu dabar muat vekannizkar bapposeqim. veamarti taam nakon laakilat dagim beshabbat: ki haddagim nibreu min hammayim, abal behemot nibreu min heapar vekannizkar bemidrash rabba. veyadua ki seder haarba yesodot lemala hu kak: mayim, esh, rucha, apar, ukemo shekkatab rabbenu za"l beshaar maamre rz"l, dap y"b, ammud b, bebeur maamar pesiotayv shel abraham abinu; yeayyen sham. ubazeh perashti bs"d, dibre rabbenu za"l b"tz-chayyim", shaar nu"n, pereq ', haqqushya shennitqashshu sham. ulepi dibre rabnet za"l shellemala, hasseder hu, mayim qodem esh - nitpareshu debarayv b"tz-chayyim" heteb. ek sheyyihyeh – nimtza, lemala, hammayim hu elyon, velaken haddagim beshabbat adipe mibbesar behema shennibrea miyyesod hattachton, dehaddagim nibreu min hammayim shehu yesod haelyon, vehashshabbat nizzon mimmaqom elyon vegabohha meod. veod perashti, bs"d, taam acher, al pi mah shekkatab bammidrash bereshit-rabba, pereq z', siman b, beubda deyaaqob ish kepar nibraay, shehora betzor shehaddagim teunim shechita, veshama rabbi chaggay, veshalach acharayv vehilqahu veku', vehebi lo rabbi chaggay reaya min hattora, diktib (bammidbar y,kb): "hatzon ubaqar yishshachet lahem umatza lahem, im kol dege hayyam yeasep lahem umatza lahem". mikkan reaya: tzon ubaqar bae shechita, udege hayyam, day lahem baasipa min hayyam; yeayyen sham. ubazeh muban heteb hattaam deokelin dagim beshabbat, lehorot, kemo shehaddagim, en tzarik letiqqun shellahem maaseh melaka, ken hashshabbat, en tzarik labberurim shello tiqqun "y maaseh umelaka.

clarification.explanation: It is a commandment to eat fish at all three Sabbath meals, even a little. Rabbi Yosef Chaim explains the reason: fish were created from water, whereas animals were created from earth, and the order of the four elements above is: water, fire, air, earth — that is, water is the highest element. Therefore fish, created from water (the highest element), are preferable to the meat of animals created from the lowest element (earth), and the Sabbath is nourished from a high and supernal place. Another reason Rabbi Yosef Chaim gives is based on a midrash which rules that fish do not require slaughter like animals (it suffices to gather them from the sea), from which he derives that eating fish on the Sabbath alludes to the fact that just as fish need no "repair" through an act of labor (slaughter), so too the Sabbath itself needs no repair through action and labor.
takeaways: It is a commandment to eat fish at all three Sabbath meals, even a little
A kabbalistic reason: fish were created from water, the highest of the four elements, and are therefore fitting for the Sabbath, which is nourished from a supernal place
Another reason: fish require no slaughter (labor-based repair), just as the Sabbath itself requires no repair through labor

paragraphs: Mi shenneenas velo akal seuda rishona belel shabbat, yokal shelosha seudot bayyom, vegam seudat hattashlumin yokal bah pat, visadder shulchano kemo seudat hachiyyub shel hallayla; veken hu haddin beyom tob yaaseh ken. veayin "magen-abraham", siman rtz" ushear acharonim za"l, sham. veim shalechu leadam ezeh debar maakol sheyyoklennu beshabbat, lo yoklennu bechol, vezehu mimmiddat chasidut (misseper chasidut ttsv), vekannizkar beshulchan aruk lehaggaon rabbenu zalman za"l, besiman rs"b, seip ch; yeayyen sham.

clarification.explanation: One who was prevented by circumstances and did not manage to eat the first meal on Sabbath night should make it up and eat three meals during the day, and at the meal of make-up he should also eat bread and arrange his table as at the obligatory night meal; the same law applies on a festival. If someone sent a person a special food in honor of the Sabbath, it is proper, as a matter of piety, that he not eat it during the week but save it for the Sabbath.
takeaways: One who missed the Sabbath night meal due to circumstances makes it up during the day with bread, setting the table fully as at night
A food sent in honor of the Sabbath should, as a matter of piety, be saved for the Sabbath rather than eaten during the week

paragraphs: Tob sheyyilmod al hashshulchan belel-shabbat arba peraqim rishonim shel mishna deshabbat, vehashshear yigmor bayyom. veim qasheh alayv hallimmud belel-shabbat, yilmod lepachot pereq echad vekannizkar beshaar hakkavvanot. vetob lomar dibre-tora libne beto belel-shabbat al inyan happarasha, veken haya minhago shel ateret rashe abba mari zlh"h bearbaa peraqim bammishna ubedibre tora al hashshulchan.

clarification.explanation: It is good to study, at the table on Sabbath night, the first four chapters of tractate Shabbat (Mishnah), and complete the rest during the day. One for whom studying on Sabbath night is difficult should study at least one chapter. It is likewise good to say words of Torah to the household about the matters of the parasha on Sabbath night, and so Rabbi Yosef Chaim's father was accustomed to do — teaching four chapters of Mishnah and saying words of Torah at the table.
takeaways: It is good to study the first four chapters of tractate Shabbat at the table on Sabbath night (or at least one chapter)
It is also good to say words of Torah to the household about the parasha on Sabbath night

paragraphs: Achar birkat hammazon tachazor laqach shette aguddot hahadas bishte yadeka utechabberem yachad vetomar: "zakor veshamor bedibbur echad neemru", veaach"k tebarek vetaricha, vekannizkar bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l beshaar hakkavvanot. venireh li shetztzarik lehasir hahadas achar qiddush, shekkebar berak alayv, ulehitzniu bemaqom acher, kede sheyyukal lahabio achar birkat hammazon ulebarek alayv shenit, abal lo yishshaer lepanayv, ap al gab debirkat hammazon chashib silluq - ha ikka pelugta bazeh. ulepi daat rabbenu haari"y za"l, minhag tob liqrot bekol lel-shabbat achar birkat hammazon hammishna demasseket erubin; veanu lo nahagnu bazeh; umi sheepshar lo, tabo alayv beraka.

clarification.explanation: After Grace After Meals, one again takes the two bundles of myrtle in both hands, joins them, and says "Remember and Observe were said in a single utterance," and then recites the blessing over the myrtle and smells it, as the Ari taught. Rabbi Yosef Chaim adds that the myrtle should be removed after Kiddush (over which the blessing was already recited then) and set aside elsewhere, so that it can be brought again after Grace After Meals and the blessing recited over it a second time — rather than leaving it in front of him throughout the whole meal (there is a dispute as to whether Grace After Meals is considered an interruption for this purpose). Also, according to the Ari, it is a good custom to read, every Sabbath night after Grace After Meals, the Mishnah of tractate Eruvin, even though this was not their custom at home — and one who can practice this, blessing will come upon him.
takeaways: After Grace After Meals, the blessing over the myrtle is recited again and it is smelled, after having been set aside and not left on the table since Kiddush
There is a custom (not followed by Rabbi Yosef Chaim) of studying the Mishnah of tractate Eruvin on Sabbath night after Grace After Meals

paragraphs: Minhag rabbenu haari"y za"l lehannicha hashshulchan bimqomo belel-shabbat achar birkat hammazon, vehammappa perusa alayv, vekos shel beraka gam ken munnach alayv, vehaya mashir bo meat yayin kede lehashir sham birkat lel-shabbat besod "asuk shemen" haamur beelisha hannabi alayv hashshalom (melakim b d,b) kakkatub bazzohar haqqadosh. vegam lesibba zo, haya meshayyer tachat mappa happerusa meat petitin shel pat, abal lo lechem shalem vekannizkar beshaar hakkavvanot, ak tzarik lishmor zeh min hachatulim hammetzuyim babbayit shello yikkanesu veyoklu happat. vehannizhar bekol hannizkar leel, tabo alayv beraka.

clarification.explanation: The Ari was accustomed to leave the table in its place on Sabbath night after Grace After Meals, with the cloth spread over it and the cup of blessing placed on it, leaving a little wine in the cup in order to preserve the blessing of the Sabbath night, according to the secret of the "flask of oil" in the story of Elisha the Prophet (2 Kings 4), as explained in the holy Zohar. For a similar reason, he was accustomed to leave a few bread crumbs (not a whole loaf) under the spread cloth — but one must be careful of cats that might come in and eat the bread that was left.
takeaways: It is customary to leave the table set with a little wine and some bread crumbs after Grace After Meals on Sabbath night, according to a secret that preserves the blessing of the Sabbath
One must be careful that cats do not reach the bread that was left

paragraphs: Inyan hazzivvug vehaoneh shel shabbat hu metzuvveh rabba, veashre hazzokeh laasot kol maasayv leshem shamayim. ukebar ameru rabbotenu zikronam libraka baggemara (ketubbot sb:): onatan shel talmide chakamim, millel-shabbat lelel-shabbat; veraq belel rishon shel pesach, velel rosh-hashshana, velel shemini-atzeret, velel sheni dishbuot, apillu shechalu beshabbat, en laasot zivvug bahem "p hassod, ella raq im hu lel tebilat metzuvveh. vekol zeh hu letalmade chakamim veanshe maaseh, abal hamon haam, mi sheyyodea beatzmo sheeno yakol laamod bedabar zeh, sheeno yakol likbosh taavato, muttar lo leshammesh apillu belelot hachol, veraq chayyab lehizzaher liprosh samuk levistah. vegam beona shel lel-shabbat shehi metzuvva gedola enah metzuvva min hammubchar, ella raq im yeshammesh achar chatzot layla. nimtzeta atta lamed, arbaa madregot yesh betashmish hammitta: harishon haggarua, hu hamshammesh bimot hachol qodem chatzot layla; vehashsheni hamulleh mimmennu, hu hamshammesh bechol achar chatzot layla; vehashshelishi hamulleh mimmennu, hamshammesh belel-shabbat qodem chatzot; veharebii hamulleh mikkullam, hamshammesh belel-shabbat achar chatzot. veim nizdammen lo tebilat metzuvveh belele hachol, hare zeh meshammesh beotah layla ap al pi shehu chasid uparush, veeno rashshay leakkebah ad lel-shabbat; veoseh bazeh tiqqun kemo ona shel lel-shabbat, vekidmukach mehazzohar haqqadosh (ch" n.), deetzlo nechshab lel tebila kelil shabbat; velaken tob sheyyizzaher leqayyemah gam ken achar chatzot layla heka deepshar lo, abal im choshesh pen chas vechalila yireh qeri im yashen qodem tashmish, hare zeh meshammesh qodem shena, apillu qodem chatzot. vegam belele rosh chodesh veyom tob yesh maala bezivvug al pi hassod, vachasidim veanshe maaseh meqayyemim bahem mitzvat ona.

Veda deita beseper "peri-etz-chayyim" vezeh leshono: mori zlh"h haya omer, dekol azhara "meereb shabbat leereb shabbat", hu bimshammesh leshem herayon, letzorek banim; vetzarik lihyot az hazzivvug kede sheyyishreh behay tippa neshama qedosha elyona mehazzivvug haelyon, abal im ishto kebar meubberet o meniqa, en lachush alayv kol kak; vehattaam, ki kol atzmah shel azhara zo enah ella lebal yashpia neshamot hanniqraim "tzaddiq vera lo", raq neshamot deshabbat kannizkar, abal im hi kebar meubberet o meniqa, batela taana zo; ad kan leshon morenu harab chayyim veyittol za"l sham; yeayyen sham. veod raiti lerabbenu harab chayyim veyittol za"l b"olat-tamid", dap s"t, ammud , sheddiqdeq min ha"tiqqunim", sop dap tz"g kepi hachilluq hannizkar, deyesh lechalleq bimubberet o meniqa; yeayyen sham. vbsh"q "mqbtzl" katabti bs"d, deen setira middebarim hannizkar lemah shekkatab rabbenu za"l beshaar taame hammitzvot ubeshaar hakkavvanot beinyan hazzivvug shel yemot hachol. vekatabti, d"g degam talmide chakam yekolim lismok al dibre morenu harab chayyim veyittol za"l beseper "peri-etz-chayyim" hannizkar, leshammesh bechol bimubberet umeniqa, im kol zeh rauy sheyyinhagu biprishut velo yargilu atzmam bekak, veraq im bederek miqreh nizdammen lahem dabar zeh bechol, en lachush.

clarification.explanation: The marital duty (conjugal relations) on Sabbath night is a great commandment. The Sages established that the conjugal schedule of Torah scholars is from Sabbath night to Sabbath night, except for a few special nights (Passover, Rosh Hashanah, Shemini Atzeret, Shavuot) on which relations should not be had according to the esoteric tradition, unless it is the night of immersion (emerging from niddah). All this applies to Torah scholars and men of piety, but an ordinary person who knows he cannot control his inclination is permitted to have relations on weeknights as well, provided he is careful to abstain close to his wife's menstrual period. There are also gradations within fulfilling the commandment on Sabbath night itself: the most preferable is to fulfill it after midnight. It thus emerges that there are four levels: the worst of all — on a weekday before midnight; better than that — on a weekday after midnight; better than that — on the Sabbath before midnight; and the best of all — on the Sabbath after midnight. One who has a night of obligatory immersion during the week (his wife emerging from niddah) must fulfill the duty that same night and not postpone it to the Sabbath, since this is considered a repair just like the Sabbath conjugal duty. If he is concerned about a seminal emission should he sleep before relations, he should fulfill it even before midnight. The nights of Rosh Chodesh and festivals also have a special virtue according to the esoteric tradition, and the pious are careful to fulfill the duty on them. It is further brought in the name of Rabbi Chaim Vital: the warning of "from Sabbath eve to Sabbath eve" is directed mainly at one who intends to have children, so that a supernal soul rest in the drop; but if the wife is already pregnant or nursing, there is not such strict care about this matter, although it is proper that even then one practice some restraint.
takeaways: The conjugal schedule of Torah scholars is from Sabbath night to Sabbath night; an ordinary person who cannot control his inclination is permitted on weekdays too, subject to the rules of distancing around menstruation
The most preferable time to fulfill the marital duty on the Sabbath is after midnight
A night of obligatory immersion (emerging from niddah) during the week overrides waiting for the Sabbath — it must be fulfilled immediately
According to Rabbi Chaim Vital, the strictness of "from Sabbath eve to Sabbath eve" is mainly for one intending to have children; for a pregnant or nursing wife the matter is more lenient

paragraphs: Apillu bechadeshe haibbur vechadeshe yeniqa, vaapillu ishah aqara, o sheppasequ dameha, sheenah reuya leholid od, chayyab balah leqayyem mitzvat ona bah; vaapillu shehu chakam vechasid, eno rashshay lebattel mimmenna mitzvat ona; veal yachshob shebbeilato tihyeh lebattala, ella beemet gam beilot ellu osim peri lemala, veyivvaledu mehem neshamot; vekamporash bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l beshaar taame hammitzvot veza"l: abotenu, abraham, yitzchaq veyaaqob, hagam ki hayu neshotehem aqarot - lo hayu nimnaim min hazzivvug, vehayu mekavvenim el zivvug hattediri veku'; yeayyen sham. vehaggaon chida" za"l b"midbar-qedemot", dap p"g, min zohar haqqadosh biktabit yad vezeh leshono: amar rabbi shimon: leolam yeqayyem adam mitzvat ona bezugato leshem shamayim, shekkol otam veku', ap shehi aqara uzeqena, enam holekim leibbud, ella hqb"h metzuvveh lammalak hammunneh sheyyishmerem leatid labo, veyihyeh lo banim rabbim veku'; yeayyen sham.

clarification.explanation: Even during the months of pregnancy or nursing, and even with a barren woman or one who has already stopped menstruating (who will not give birth again), the husband is obligated to fulfill the marital duty with her, and even if he is a scholar and pious man, he may not forgo it. One should not think that such relations are in vain, for even from them "fruit" is produced above and souls are born from them, as explained in the words of the Ari that our forefathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob did not refrain from relations with their wives even though they were barren, with the intention of "the constant union" (a permanent, ongoing union, not only for the purpose of procreation). It is likewise brought in the name of the holy Zohar that the Holy One, blessed be He, preserves the fruit of these unions for the future to come.
takeaways: The obligation of the marital duty applies also to a pregnant, nursing, barren wife, or one who has stopped menstruating — it may not be forgone
According to the esoteric tradition, souls are born above even from these unions, and they are not in vain

paragraphs: Tob sheyyitten adam mittato ben tzapon ledarom ukemo sheameru chakamenu zikronam libraka, veyihyeh dugmat adam harishon keshennibra. vekak yaaseh: rosho lammizrach, keneged haddaat hanniqra "mizrach", diktib: "mimmizrach abi zaraka"; veraglayv lammaarab, keneged yesod umalkut; veyado hayyemanit baddarom, shehu hachesed; veyad hassemalit batztzapon, shehu haggebura, vekannizkar bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l, shaar taame hammitzvot, dap v, ammud b; ayyen sham. vetzarik lishhot al habbeten ad sheyyiklu tippot hazzera legamre, veken yizzaher leachar sheshshimmesh mittato apillu meotam hattippot shehem kemo mayim veenam qeshurot keloben betza, ki kol zeh biklal hashchatat hazzera, ukemo shekkatab rabbenu za"l beshaar taame hammitzvot, dap z, ammud b; yeayyen sham. mihu, nireh li deeno neenash alehem, kevan dehu anus bazeh mitztzad qiyyum hammitzva. veyadua ki etzel rob bene-adam enam nipsaqim nitzotzot ellu raq achar sheyyashtin, al-ken yishtaddel lehashtin, velo yitbol qodem sheyyashtin; vekavvanat rabbenu za"l lehazhiro bazeh.

clarification.explanation: It is good for a person to place his bed in a north-south orientation, following the example of Adam at his creation: his head to the east (corresponding to the attribute of Da'at, called "east"), his feet to the west (corresponding to Yesod and Malchut), his right hand to the south (corresponding to Chesed), and his left hand to the north (corresponding to Gevurah) — as the Ari taught. After marital relations one should remain on his stomach until the drops of semen have completely finished, and should also be careful about the liquid drops (which are not yet bound like the white of an egg), which are also included in the prohibition of destroying seed. Nevertheless, Rabbi Yosef Chaim holds that one is not punished for these, since he is forced into this in the course of fulfilling the commandment itself. Since for most people these drops stop only after urinating, it is good to urinate before immersing.
takeaways: The recommended orientation of the bed: head to the east, feet to the west, right hand to the south, left hand to the north, corresponding to the allusions of the sefirot
After relations one should remain on his stomach until all the drops of semen have finished, and should urinate before immersing

paragraphs: Asur leshammesh leor hanner, veeno maspiq netinat mechitztzat sedinim shel pishtan sebib hammitta, ella tzarik shello yihyeh or hanner meir betok hammitta kelal veiqqar, ukemo shekkatab rabbenu za"l beshaar taame hammitzvot, dap z', ammud ; y"sh. umilleshon rabbotenu za"l mukach, deim yashen beaksadra gedola, o al gag gadol, vehanner rachoq min hammitta, veen maggia oro lemitta kelal, shari, "p shehu roeh beenayv et hanner haddoleq. umah shekkatab haggaon morenu harab shelomoh qeluger za"l, deim meshammesh bekissuy shel sadin gadol verachab, shari - en debarayv mechuvvarin, vekaasher hissagtiv bitshuba. veish veishto sheyyesh lahem yeled qatan yoneq, vishenim bacheder, vetzarik lahem or bacheder, shello tukal lehaniq bachoshek, ketzad yaaseh beshabbat, sheeno yakol lekabbot qodem tashmisho ulehadliqo achar kak? asiti lahem taqqana - sheyyannichu hanner betok challon amoq heasuy bakkotel, veyaasu lachallon delet, ubeet tashmish yistom haddelet velo yireh or hanner bacheder, veachar tashmish yiptachennu kede shettaniq haishsha leoro.

Veda ki hamminhag pashut poh irenu bagdad y" mizzeman qadmon, dehechatan shennose betula, meshammesh belel chuppa shehi bia rishona, leor hanner, apillu hu chakam vechasid, bilti shum piqpuq. vaani amarti taam lehetter zeh bebia rishona shehi enah reuya leibbur, deen haishsha mitabberet mibbia rishona (yebamot ld.), ki im raq hi laasotah keli, velaken en hachitzonim mitgarim bazeh, veen kan onesh shel banim nikpim deameru rabbotenu za"l, yaan ki oto tashmish eno rauy leherayon, ki inyan zeh hu segulli veha talya beha. veda ki or hanner hu chamur meor hallebana, veiqqar hannezeq yihyeh meor hanner davqa; mihu, im or hallebana zoreach behedya al hammitta, lo yeshammesh, abal im en or hallebana zoreach mammash al hammitta, "p shemmeira hammitta mikkoach or hallebana harachoq mimmenna, muttar leshammesh "y sheyyihyeh maapil besadin sheyyihyeh parus alayv legamre. ubishat haddechaq, shehu tzarik lashshammash, veor hallebana zoreach al hammitta, veeno yakol lehamtin ad sheyyaabor haor mealeha, hare zeh maapil besadin sheyyipresenu alayv veal ishto ad sheyyihyu mekussin bo legamre veshari. vbsh"q "mqbtzl" heeleti, deim ala ammud-hashshachar, kol zeman shello heir hayyom, shehu techillat lebishat tepillin bechol, chashib biklal layla umuttar lo leshammesh, veen zeh biklal meshammesh mittato bayyom. veyishtaddel haadam litbol achar tashmish-hammitta, ubiprat beyom shabbat, kede sheyyeqabbel tosepet shabbat shel hayyom begup tahor.

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to have marital relations by candlelight, and it is not enough to hang a sheet as a curtain around the bed — rather, the candlelight must not illuminate inside the bed at all. If one sleeps in a large place (such as a covered porch or a wide roof) and the candle is far enough that its light does not reach the bed at all, it is permitted, even if he can see the lit candle burning in the distance. Rabbi Yosef Chaim disagrees with those who permitted relying on merely covering with a wide sheet while the candle is nearby and shining. For a couple with a nursing infant who need light in the room, Rabbi Yosef Chaim offers a solution: to place the candle inside a deep window recess in the wall with a door, closing the door during relations and opening it afterward for nursing. In Baghdad the established custom is that a groom marrying a virgin has relations by candlelight on the wedding night (the first intercourse), even if he is a scholar and pious man, since the first intercourse does not cause pregnancy (and therefore carries no such concern) — and is therefore permitted even by candlelight. Moonlight is more lenient than candlelight; if the moon shines directly on the bed, one should not have relations; and in a case of pressing need, when one cannot wait for the light to pass, he should cover himself and his wife completely with a sheet. And if the moonlight does not shine directly on the bed, even though the bed is lit by its distant light, it is permitted, but even then by means of a sheet spread completely over them. It was also ruled that from the break of dawn (before daylight, the beginning of the time for putting on tefillin) it is still considered night and relations are permitted. One should try to immerse after marital relations, especially on the Sabbath, in order to receive the additional measure of the Sabbath day in a pure body.
takeaways: It is forbidden to have relations by candlelight that illuminates the bed, but it is permitted if the candle is far away and does not illuminate the bed at all, even if visible from a distance

Direct moonlight on the bed: one should not have relations; only in a case of pressing need, when one cannot wait, should he cover himself and his wife completely with a sheet. If it is not direct, it is permitted, but still with a sheet spread over them
Baghdad custom: a groom has relations on the wedding night (first intercourse) even by candlelight, since it does not cause pregnancy
It is good to immerse after relations, especially on the Sabbath, to receive the day's holiness in purity
